scope: References used by ProxyComparativeEvidence.tsx. Merge references as additions and updates by their existing canonical id. No shared bibliography edited by this subtask.

references.title: Concordance of the toxicity of pharmaceuticals in humans and in animals
references.finding: For 150 pharmaceuticals selected for known human toxicity, animal studies showed concordance with 71% of 221 human toxicity events in at least one species. This is not a generic positive-animal-to-human transfer probability.
references.verification: Primary PubMed abstract: 12 companies, 150 compounds, 221 human toxicity events, rodent/nonrodent concordance denominators and direction checked.

references.authors: Ineichen BV, Furrer E, Grüninger SL, Zürrer WE, Macleod MR
references.title: Analysis of animal-to-human translation shows that only 5% of animal-tested therapeutic interventions obtain regulatory approval for human applications
references.finding: In a selected 62-therapy subanalysis, random-effects meta-analysis compared clinical-positive and animal-positive study proportions, pooled RR 0.86 (95% CI 0.80–0.92); this is not an 86% generic replication probability. Across the broader 367-therapy umbrella review, 50% reached human studies, 40% an RCT and 5% approval.
references.verification: Publisher full text and original supplementary R script checked. Script metabin(Clin_positive, Clin_all, Pre_positive, Pre_all, ...) establishes clinical/preclinical ratio direction, despite Methods prose describing the reverse order. Subanalysis: 1496 animal studies and 515 clinical studies; 62 therapies, each at least five animal studies.

references.authors: Sumner RN, Tomlinson M, Craigon J, England GCW, Lea RG
references.title: Independent and combined effects of diethylhexyl phthalate and polychlorinated biphenyl 153 on sperm quality in the human and dog
references.finding: In vitro sperm experiments in nine human donors and eleven dogs found DNA-fragmentation responses and chemical interactions under DEHP and PCB153 exposure. Human motility did not significantly respond to either chemical alone; mixtures altered it. This is a paired cross-species chemical experiment, not an electromagnetic exposure study.
references.verification: Primary full text XML via Europe PMC. Four-by-four dose combinations: DEHP 0, 0.75, 3.75, 37.53 µg/mL; PCB153 0, 0.26, 1.32, 13.22 ng/mL. Measurements at 10 minutes and 3 hours. Research family overlaps Lea2016.

references.title: Atrazine induces complete feminization and chemical castration in male African clawed frogs (Xenopus laevis)
references.journal: Proceedings of the National Academy of Sciences
references.finding: In this experiment, genetically male Xenopus laevis exposed to 2.5 µg/L atrazine during development showed altered reproductive development and function. The finding establishes a specified chemical intervention pathway, not a global amphibian-decline explanation.
references.verification: Primary article checked: genetic ZZ animals and 2.5 ppb exposure, reproductive endpoints. Used only to establish that a pesticide explanation is biologically applicable across species.

updates.authors: Harris IT, Maddock C, Farnworth M, Nankervis K, Perrett J, Pyatt AZ, Blanchard RN
updates.title: Temporal trends in equine sperm progressive motility: a systematic review and meta-regression
updates.finding: Meta-regression of 230 estimates from 229 articles over sample years 1984–2019 estimated progressive sperm motility declining from 63.69% to 42.35% (33.51% relative decline), slope −0.610 percentage points/year. The reported −0.96%/year is relative to the initial level. No matched RF exposure series was analysed.
updates.verification: Primary article and version-of-record author repository checked. Corrects the existing incomplete harris2023 record: title, author initials, DOI and prior unsourced −0.75%/year finding.
